newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Lower taxes drive NZ surplus outlook lower.
newsitem.headline: Lower taxes drive NZ surplus outlook lower.

text.p: The New Zealand government on Wednesday released figures showing lower than expected business tax receipts were the main reason for a cut in the expected budget surplus in the current year.
Treasury figures in the current year fiscal update showed it expected the operating surplus for the year to June 30, 1997 to be NZ$2.312 billion, $181 million lower than expected in December.
Total revenues were expected to come in lower than the December forecasts largely because of a downward revision in the expected tax take by $296 million (0.9 percent).
Business taxes were forecast to be down $334 million while household taxes would rise by $38 million, Treasury said.
Company tax showed an even sharper fall, down $566 million or 14.2 percent from December forecasts.
Treasury said lower company tax forecasts were the result of lower terminal tax revenue from the 1995/96 year and lower than expected profit growth through 1996/97.
Net public debt was lower by $576 million at $25.5 billion largely because of a change in timing of the Equiticorp appeal hearing and lower expenditure on physical assets.
The Crown has had a court judgement lodged against it of $328 million, following the collapse of investment company Equiticorp. It is appealing the decision.
